subject: Electrical Engineering
title: State-Space: The Matrix Approach
description: A short lesson to help you apply State-Space: The Matrix Approach.

hook.text: Transfer functions describe input-output. State-space describes everything happening inside the system.

buildup.text: State variables capture the system's internal condition — positions, velocities, temperatures, currents.

discovery.text: The state equation: ẋ = Ax + Bu. The output equation: y = Cx + Du. Four matrices define the system.

twist.text: State-space handles multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems easily — transfer functions can't.

climax.text: Aerospace, robotics, and modern control design all prefer state-space representation.

punchline.text: Four matrices, full picture — state-space reveals the internals.

quiz.question: What advantage does state-space have over transfer functions?
options: It uses simpler math with no matrices
It naturally handles multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems
It works only with digital systems
